_comment: Recruits. tier: field (can fight on missions), core (deep bonds), recruit (light). Stats 1-10: might, craft, lore, charm, grit. start: in the roster on a new game. locked_party: always in the party (Ash). Traits are defined below. post: where they stand in Hollowmark when not governing, in the party or injured. look: paper-doll outfit and colors (placeholders until the PixelLab pass). lines: what they say when you talk to them in town. quips: one-liners for expedition reports. join: how someone not on the starting roster is found (claim, building, standing, research, renown, bond, rescue); when it is met they wait at the south gate until hired for their hire price (rescues join straight from the expedition). rumour: what the Newcomers screen (N) says before they turn up. pitch: what they say at the gate. welcome: what they say when they join.

greedy.name: Greedy
greedy.desc: Skims, but squeezes harder. +2 Gilt as governor.

stubborn.name: Stubborn
stubborn.desc: Will not give an inch. Governs with 1 more Fray resistance.

coward.name: Coward
coward.desc: Flees the edge. Governs with 1 less Fray resistance.

bookish.name: Bookish
bookish.desc: Happier with paper than people. Counts double at the Scriptorium.

ex_concord.name: Ex-Concord
ex_concord.desc: Knows the forms. The Concord hates them for it.

flirt.name: Flirt
flirt.desc: Charm counts double with envoys and in the tavern.

night_owl.name: Night Owl
night_owl.desc: Does their best work after dark.

ink_sick.name: Ink-sick
ink_sick.desc: The Blank got a taste once. Lore +2, but never fully well.

unwritten.name: Unwritten
unwritten.desc: No Ledger entry. The Blank treats them oddly. Leads every mission.

contract.name: Contracted
contract.desc: Paid by the job. Fights harder for coin, sulks without it.

recruits.name: Ash
recruits.title: the Unwritten
recruits.blurb: Spat back out by the Blank with no name, no voice and no Ledger entry. Everyone projects something different onto the silence.

recruits.name: Brannoc "Bran" Tolley
recruits.title: mercenary
recruits.blurb: His contract is tattooed on his arm and tightens if he breaks it. Will sell you out if outbid, and tells you so.
quips: Bran has submitted an invoice for "hazard, emotional".
Bran asks that it be noted he was "the competent one".
lines: Contract says I guard you. Doesn't say I have to like the town.
Point me at something and pay me. That's the whole relationship.
If someone offers me more, you'll hear it from me first. Professional courtesy.

recruits.name: Edwin "Quill" Pask
recruits.title: quartermaster
recruits.blurb: Kept Hollowmark's books for the Concord. Now cooks them for you. Knows where every coin is buried, and who buried it.
quips: Quill kept receipts for everything, including the weather.
Quill has filed the trip under "deductible".
lines: Every coin in Hollowmark has a story. Most of them end with me.
The Concord taught me bookkeeping. I taught it creativity.
Ask me about the ledger. Actually, don't. Read it yourself at the table{tag:ledger}.

recruits.name: Old Tobble
recruits.title: tavern keeper
recruits.blurb: Has been about to retire for thirty years. Hears everything; sells most of it.
quips: Tobble complained about his knees for the entire trip, then outran everyone.
Tobble sold the story to three different drinkers before the report was even written.
lines: Retiring next week. Have been since before your mother was written.
First drink's free. The second one costs you a secret.
People talk after dark. I listen. Then I charge.

recruits.name: Pell Mossop
recruits.title: gravedigger
recruits.blurb: Digs too fast. Nobody has asked why the graves are always ready before anyone dies.
quips: Pell dug a hole at every campsite. Nobody asked what for. Nobody wanted to know.
Pell measured everyone on the way home. "Just in case."
lines: Dug three this morning. Nobody's died yet. Give it time.
The Blank doesn't leave bodies. Bad for business.
You've got a good shape for a grave. Compliment, that.

recruits.name: Mother Gristle
recruits.title: hedge-witch
recruits.blurb: Heals the party and bills them for it. Her poisons and her medicines are the same bottles.
recruits.rumour: A hedge-witch in the Gutterwoods is in trouble with her own coven. She would owe you. She would also bill you.
quips: Mother Gristle has billed the squad for "moral support".
Mother Gristle collected some mushrooms. She says they are for cooking. She did not say whose.
lines: This one cures fever. That one causes it. Same price.
I bill by the wound. You look expensive.

recruits.name: Corporal Daro
recruits.title: "Ninefingers", deserter
recruits.blurb: Deserted the Concord army rather than strike out a village. Sharpest tongue in the Inklands.
recruits.rumour: A Concord deserter is hiding somewhere along the Tithe Road with a price on their head. They have opinions about the price.
quips: Daro saluted a scarecrow out of habit, then threatened it.
Daro wants it on record that the plan was bad and they followed it anyway.
lines: Lost the finger to a form. Long story. Paperwork was involved.
The Concord strikes out villages with a pen. I prefer the sword. More honest.

recruits.name: Sister Hild
recruits.title: runaway scribe
recruits.blurb: Ran from the Abbey with one stolen page that rewrites itself every night.
recruits.rumour: A runaway scribe is hiding up in Wickham with a page the Abbey wants back.
quips: Sister Hild's page rewrote itself as a shopping list. Everything on it was found.
Sister Hild says the trip was "very loud, in the quiet way".
lines: The page rewrote itself again. Last night it said your name. You don't have one.
Ink-sickness isn't so bad. The voices are mostly polite.

recruits.name: Hetty Coyne
recruits.title: cartographer
recruits.blurb: Maps places a week before they exist. Her maps of the Blank are blank, which she finds professionally insulting.
recruits.rumour: Someone up in the Wickham Hills is drawing roads that aren't there yet. Claim the Hills and you can ask her why.
recruits.pitch: I mapped this town a week before your gate went up. You have a road in the wrong place. Take me on and I'll tell you which.
recruits.welcome: Wonderful. I've already drawn my desk. It's in your hall, so you'd better build one.
quips: Hetty mapped the route home before they left. It was right, which bothered everyone.
Hetty refused to walk anywhere she hadn't drawn yet. She drew very quickly.
lines: This map's a week ahead. In a week there's a bridge here. Don't ask me who builds it.
I tried to map the Blank. Seven sheets of nothing. Best work I've ever done.
If I run, follow me. I always know the way out. I drew it first.

recruits.name: Dunmore Vellacott
recruits.title: debt-tattooed blacksmith
recruits.blurb: Every debt he owes is tattooed on his skin, by law. He has run out of arms and started on his back.
recruits.rumour: A smith who owes money to half the Inklands wants steady work. Barracks need blades. Build one and he'll come knocking.
recruits.pitch: You built barracks. Barracks need steel, and I need to pay off my left shoulder. Twenty-five Gilt and I'm yours.
recruits.welcome: Good. Write it here, under the one for the horse. No, the other horse.
quips: Dunmore fixed everyone's boots on the road and charged them for it. Then paid it all to a debt collector who was waiting at the gate.
Dunmore says the trip was worth "about a forearm".
lines: See this one? Owe a man a pig. He's dead now. Still owe it.
I can mend a blade, a hinge or a grudge. The grudge costs extra.
When I'm out of skin, the debts go to my next of kin. Lucky them.

recruits.name: Jessamy Leake
recruits.title: smuggler
recruits.blurb: Only moves cargo after dark, and never asks what's in the crates. Asks a lot about you, though.
recruits.rumour: The Mercenary Guild has a night runner they only lend to friends. Get the Guild to Friendly and she'll come and look you over.
recruits.pitch: The Guild says you're good for it. I like people who are good for it. Forty Gilt, and I'll bring in anything you want. After dark.
recruits.welcome: Lovely. I'll take the room with the window that doesn't lock. Don't wait up.
quips: Jessamy came back with a crate nobody remembers loading. She says not to open it until spring.
Jessamy flirted past three checkpoints and a goat.
lines: Day's for honest folk. I sleep through it, mostly out of respect.
You've got a lovely face for a crime. That's a compliment where I'm from.
Don't ask what's in the crates. I don't. It keeps us both cheerful.

recruits.name: Mr. Biscuits
recruits.title: a dog, possibly
recruits.blurb: The Coven's familiar. Might be a dog that walks like a man, might be a man under a very old curse. Answers to both, and to "walkies".
recruits.rumour: The Gutterwood Coven keeps a familiar that sniffs out the Blank. Become Friendly with them and they might lend him out.
recruits.pitch: Woof. (The Coven says you're friends now. Friends get Mr. Biscuits. No charge. Treats are, however, expected.)
recruits.welcome: (He spins round three times and lies down at your feet. That seems to be a yes.)
quips: Mr. Biscuits barked at the edge of the Blank all night. In the morning it had moved back a little.
Mr. Biscuits buried something at every campsite. Pell has gone to find out what.
lines: Woof. (He looks at the white on the horizon and growls, very quietly.)
(He offers you a paw. It is definitely a hand. Wearing a glove. Probably.)
Wrrf. (Translation, according to Pell: "the graves are too shallow".)

recruits.name: The Merrow Three
recruits.title: orphan choir
recruits.blurb: Pim, Pet and Posy share one voice between them, passed round like a hot coal. When they sing in the margins, the Blank holds its breath.
recruits.rumour: Three orphans have been heard singing at the edge of the Blank. Write wards into the margins (Research: Margin Wards) and they'll follow the tune.
recruits.pitch: (Pim:) We heard your margins singing. (Pet:) Badly. (Posy:) We could teach them. We just need a roof and some soup.
recruits.welcome: (All three, in one voice:) Thank you. (Then three voices, arguing about beds.)
quips: The Merrow Three sang the squad to sleep. Nobody remembers falling asleep. Nobody remembers the song.
Pim had the voice for most of the trip. Posy is not speaking to her. Literally.
lines: (Pim:) It's my turn with the voice. (Pet, silently, disagrees.)
(Posy:) The Blank doesn't like harmony. Too many parts. It can't swallow them all at once.
(Pet:) We used to be four. We don't talk about it. We don't have the voice to spare.

recruits.name: Odile Penhallow
recruits.title: tax collector with a conscience
recruits.blurb: Collected tithes for the Concord until she was told to collect a village. Quit on the spot, with the ledger.
recruits.rumour: A Concord tax collector quit with a ledger the Concord very much wants back. She's waiting to see if Hollowmark is worth defecting to. Earn 3 Renown.
recruits.pitch: I've heard of you, which means the Concord has too. I brought their ledger. Thirty Gilt for my severance and it's yours. So am I.
recruits.welcome: I've already found four mistakes in your books. Two of them are in your favour. I'll fix the other two.
quips: Odile taxed a bandit. He paid. He seemed confused about why.
Odile kept a running tally of everything the squad owed each other. It has been framed in the tavern.
lines: They told me to collect a village. Not from. Collect. I took the ledger and ran.
Your books are a disgrace. I love them. So much to do.
Quill and I disagree about rounding. Quill rounds up. For Quill.

recruits.name: Big Ottoline
recruits.title: cabaret bouncer
recruits.blurb: Tobble's niece, or cousin, or creditor. Threw a Concord magistrate through a door and then charged him for the door.
recruits.rumour: Old Tobble knows a bouncer who might work for free, if he likes you enough to ask her. Get close to Tobble (bond rank 2).
recruits.pitch: Uncle Tobble says you're all right. He's never said that about anyone. I'll keep your door. Nobody gets through it I don't like.
recruits.welcome: Rule one: no fighting in my tavern. Rule two: if there is fighting, I win it.
quips: Ottoline carried the injured home two at a time and complained it was a light day.
Ottoline stood in a doorway at the inn and nobody tried to rob the squad. Nobody tried to leave either.
lines: Uncle Tobble says I'm the muscle. I say he's the mouth. Between us we're one bouncer.
Name's on the list or it isn't. If it isn't, I can help with that. Painfully.
Throw a magistrate through a door once and they never let you forget it.

recruits.name: Fauvette
recruits.title: cabaret duellist
recruits.blurb: Stage name of Colombe Brissot, which she will deny. Star of the Crimson Encore, where the closing act is a real duel with a paying volunteer. Knows every secret told in her dressing room, and charges for each one.
recruits.rumour: The Crimson Encore went dark when the Blank took its street. Its star duellist only performs for a crowd worth the trouble. Earn 5 Renown.
recruits.pitch: Darling, the whole Inklands is talking about you, and I hate not being the one they talk about. Sixty Gilt, and I'll fight beside you instead. Better seats.
recruits.welcome: Ottoline used to keep my door. Now she keeps yours. We'll get on famously, you and I, until one of us gets bored.
quips: Fauvette duelled a bandit chief for the road toll and bowed to the survivors. They applauded.
Fauvette came back from the expedition with three secrets, two love letters and nobody's purse but her own. She says.
lines: Every duel is a performance. The trick is making sure the other one doesn't know it's their last.
I hear things in my dressing room. You'd be amazed what people tell a woman with a sword at their throat. And what they tell her without one.
Ottoline thinks I'm reckless. I think the volunteers knew what they signed. It was printed on the ticket.

recruits.name: Sister Osyth
recruits.title: crypt-keeper
recruits.blurb: Kept the crypts under Saint Ledger's for forty years and counted the dead in them, notch by notch, on a board she carries everywhere: eleven thousand four hundred and six. The Concord says the hill was always empty. She has never agreed.
recruits.rumour: Sister Hild says the old crypt-keeper is still down under the Bonefield Cloister, counting. Somebody would have to go and fetch her.
recruits.pitch: You found me, so you can count. Good. I'll keep your dead in order if you keep your living out of my way.
recruits.welcome: Where do you bury people here? Show me. Then show me the book where you write them down.
quips: Osyth counted the dead on the road and the living in the camp. The numbers came out level, which she did not like.
Osyth came back with three new notches on her board and wouldn't say whose they were.
lines: Eleven thousand four hundred and six. I check it every night. It never goes down.
Your gravedigger's quick. Too quick. I've had a word.
Hild still owes me a candle. Tell her I've added interest.

recruits.name: Brother Cuthbert
recruits.title: bell-ringer
recruits.blurb: Rang Saint Ledger's tenor bell for twenty years, which took his hearing and gave him shoulders like a dray horse. When the Abbot ordered every hour rung at once, he walked out to the pilgrims' hostel at Scarth Pass and has been shouting at pilgrims since.
recruits.rumour: A deaf monk keeps the pilgrims' hostel at Scarth Pass and rings a hand-bell at anything that moves. Claim the Pass and he will hear about you, eventually.
recruits.pitch: WHAT? Oh. A job. Twenty Gilt and a bell. Any bell. I'm not fussy. I CAN'T HEAR FUSSY.
recruits.welcome: Where's your bell? No bell? We'll find one. A town needs a bell, or how does the white know you're awake?
quips: Cuthbert rang a cowbell at the Blank's edge all night. Nothing came near the camp. Nothing slept, either.
Cuthbert carried the heaviest pack and didn't hear a word of complaint all trip. Literally.
lines: THE BLANK HATES BELLS. I've seen it flinch. Or I think I have. I couldn't hear it flinch.
Twenty years on the tenor. Do you know what Compline sounds like from inside the bell? Neither do I. Not any more.
Father Abbot told me to ring every hour at once. I said no. He said it louder. I didn't hear him. That's how I left.

recruits.name: Nell Tapper
recruits.title: chandler
recruits.blurb: Runs the chandlery at Candleford and, since the reeve ran off with the strongbox, the town. Makes every candle the Abbey burns and has been paid late for every one of them. Has opinions about monks, Erasers and anyone who leaves a door open in a draught.
recruits.rumour: Candleford's chandler has run the lake town since the reeve fled. Hold Candleford and she might come and see what else needs lighting.
recruits.pitch: You kept them coats off my jetty, so I owe you. Twenty-five Gilt and I'll keep Hollowmark's lamps lit cheaper than anyone. I'll still charge you, mind.
recruits.welcome: Right. Who's in charge of your lamp oil? Nobody? Then I am.
quips: Nell made a dozen candles out of camp tallow and sold eleven of them to the rest of the squad.
Nell lit the camp so bright the Blank kept its distance. She billed everyone for the light.
lines: Monks burn two hundred candles a night and pay at Michaelmas. Which Michaelmas, they won't say.
Them in white burned two months of wax on my jetty. I've a list. Names, where I could get them.
Wax remembers. Every candle's got a bit of the last one in it. Like towns, that.

recruits.name: Brother Alcuin
recruits.title: Eraser defector
recruits.blurb: A novice who read one unedited page too many, ran off to the Erasers and spent a season reading drafts aloud by the pyres. Then they burned a children's primer and he came back. Still wears the white coat, with the Reader's sleeve torn off, because he says he has not earned the habit back yet.
recruits.rumour: A young brother who ran off to the Erasers has come back to the Abbey's gate and is sitting outside it. Win the Abbey's friendship and they might send him your way.
recruits.pitch: I know where the Readers camp, what they read and where Verity tells them to stand. I'd like to be useful to somebody who isn't burning anything.
recruits.welcome: Thank you. I'll take the coat off when I've earned it. Not before.
quips: Alcuin spotted a Reader's chalk mark on the road and steered the squad round it. He wouldn't say what it meant.
Alcuin read the expedition orders aloud by the fire out of habit, then went very quiet for the rest of the night.
lines: The drafts are real. That's the worst of it. Everything they read out actually happened.
First Reader Askew taught me to read old hands. Then she taught me to burn them. I kept the first lesson.
Verity came to a reading once. She knew everyone's name. She was kind. I think that's why it worked.

recruits.name: Hortense de Saulx
recruits.title: the Velvet Marquise
recruits.blurb: The Velvet Marquise: last of the de Saulx, hostess of the Causeway's best parties and its most dangerous duels. Flirts with everyone, enemies included, and means a little of it. The Concord paid her to bring you in.
recruits.rumour: A marquise on the Velvet Causeway has been asking after the person who does not exist. You will meet her at the masquerade.
recruits.pitch: I came for the party and stayed for you, sweet. Mostly for you.
recruits.welcome: Your town has a great deal of mud in it. I adore it. Where shall I sleep, and who shall I seduce first? Joking. Mostly.
quips: Hortense talked the squad past a toll-gate by complimenting the guard's moustache until he forgot his name.
Hortense came back from the expedition with every map in the camp, and a love letter from the camp.
lines: The Causeway taught me two things: how to dance, and how to leave before the music stops.
Your Bran has the manners of a dropped tray. I have decided he is charming.
Ask me anything, sweet. I will lie beautifully, and you will enjoy it.

recruits.name: Saffron Kiss
recruits.title: cabaret singer
recruits.blurb: Stage name of Maud Pickering, who was born on a coal barge and says so. Top of the bill at the Gilt Lantern on the Causeway. When she sings, things exist for a few seconds: a bridge, a chorus line, a door that was not there. She has never finished a song.
recruits.rumour: Somebody on Lantern Quay is singing a bridge across the ink every night. The bargemen say the bridge only stays up while she does.
recruits.pitch: You held the quay while I held the note. That's a duet, that is. I'm in.
recruits.welcome: Hollowmark. Hollow, mark. Hollow little town with a mark on its heart. No. Working on it.
quips: Saffron sang the camp to sleep and a fire into the grate. Nobody had lit it.
Saffron hummed the squad across a broken bridge. Halfway over she forgot the words, and they ran the rest.
lines: Every song I start turns out to be about someone. I haven't worked out who this one's about. Give it time.
Maud Pickering's the name on the coal barge. Saffron Kiss is the name on the bill. You can call me either, love, so long as you pay.
When I stop singing, the thing goes away. The bridge, the chorus girl. People an' all, sometimes. So I try not to stop.

recruits.name: Nan Cripps
recruits.title: grifter, and her shadow Tally
recruits.blurb: A Marches grifter working the Causeway: cards, contracts, word-futures and anything else that sells before it is checked. Her shadow, Tally, talks, signs the contracts she has no intention of honouring, and is the honest one. He hates that.
recruits.rumour: Somebody is selling netted words at Pendower Shallows, by the pound, with a written guarantee. The guarantee is signed by a shadow.
recruits.pitch: Nan Cripps, at your service. Reasonable rates. Tally, tell them the rates are reasonable.
recruits.welcome: Lovely town. Honest faces. I'll have most of them by Thursday. Joke! Tally, laugh.
quips: Nan won the squad's supper off a toll-keeper at cards. Tally says she cheated. Nan says Tally cheated.
Nan sold a farmer the same map twice. Tally gave him his money back the second time, and sulked all the way home.
lines: Every contract's got a loophole. I put 'em in myself. Saves time.
Tally's my shadow. He talks. He's honest. It's a terrible affliction and we're seeing someone about it.
Never trust a woman who says never trust her. That's me. Ha! Gotcha.

recruits.name: Anselme Brugière
recruits.title: vintner
recruits.blurb: Keeps the oldest presses on the Vauclair Terraces and makes the wine the masquerade has drunk for forty years. Lately it tastes of paper, and he takes that personally.
recruits.rumour: The old vintner on the Vauclair Terraces swears his grapes started tasting of paper the day the Blank came. Hold the Terraces and he may come and see whose land he is on.
recruits.pitch: Monsieur, madame, whoever: your flag is on my vines, so I am your vintner. Thirty Gilt and you will drink better than the Marquis.
recruits.welcome: Show me your cellar. You have no cellar? Then show me where you will dig one.
quips: Anselme sniffed the squad's water skins and poured two of them away. He was right about both.
Anselme traded a bottle of the '51 for a cart and a mule. He says the mule got the better of it.
lines: Wine remembers the year. This year, the wine remembers nothing. I do not like it.
The masquerade drank my wine for forty years and paid for five of them.
A good press is like a good marriage. Slow, heavy, and you must never leave it alone with the Concord.

recruits.name: Margot Vasseur
recruits.title: mask-maker
recruits.blurb: Made every mask at the masquerade for twenty years, including the Host's. Knows who wore what, and which faces were under them. Has not slept well since.
recruits.rumour: The Causeway's mask-maker has closed her shop. Friends of the Velvet Nobility say she would make masks for someone the nobles trust.
recruits.pitch: The salons say you can be trusted. Nobody in the salons can be trusted, so I came to see what that looks like.
recruits.welcome: Hold still. Everybody here needs a mask. You most of all, keeper. You have a face that shows everything.
quips: Margot made the squad masks for the road. The bandits let them pass and asked where they could buy one.
Margot sewed a torn tent in the dark by feel and then complained about the stitching.
lines: I made the Host's mask. It was a small one, at first.
A mask is not a lie. It is a lie everyone has agreed to. That is called manners.
On the Causeway you can tell a noble by the mask and a servant by the hands. Mine are a servant's.

recruits.name: Gaspard Pellerin
recruits.title: word-fisher
recruits.blurb: Nets words out of the ink at Pendower Shallows and sells them by the pound to printers and poets. Can tell a good catch from a cursed one by the smell. Has thrown back a few he will not repeat.
recruits.rumour: The word-fishers of Pendower Shallows say the catches are getting strange. Hold the Shallows and one of them might come looking for steadier work.
recruits.pitch: Your flag's on the Shallows now, so the nets are yours. Twenty-five Gilt and I'll tell you what we've been pulling out of the ink. You won't like it.
recruits.welcome: Got any ink about the place? Lake ink, the sort that wriggles. I fish words out of it, and they want feeding.
quips: Gaspard netted a word out of a puddle on the road. He wouldn't say which one. He threw it back.
Gaspard fished the squad's supper out of an ink-pond. It was a stew. Nobody asked.
lines: Last week the nets came up full of the word 'mouth'. Just that. A hundredweight of it.
Good words smell of salt. Bad ones smell of the inside of a cupboard.
The masquerade buys our best catches for their speeches. Long words, by the barrel.
